title: Armed Naxals wiped out, must identify, defeat 'dimagi' Naxals: PM in Bastar
where: Front page, continued on page 2 (Express News Service)
syllabus: GS3 › Linkages between development and spread of extremism; role of external state and non-state actors in internal security · GS3 › Security forces and agencies and their mandate · GS2 › Welfare of vulnerable sections (tribal areas) · GS4 › Inclusive and good governance
summary: Celebrating Diwali with the CRPF in Bastar, the PM said armed Naxalites have vanished from the forests but 'intellectual' Naxals remain; only seven districts were categorised as LWE-affected in a February 2026 review.
evolution: MHA review: only seven districts (five in Chhattisgarh, one each in Jharkhand and Odisha) categorised as LWE-affected.
Home Minister tells the Lok Sabha the country has become 'Naxal-free', against a March 31 target.
PM in Bastar: first Diwali 'when every district of the country is free from Naxalism'.
ideas: From security problem to near-elimination: LWE-affected districts shrank from nearly 200 in the early 2000s to 38 by end-2025 and seven in February 2026; incidents and deaths fell by over four-fifths since 2010.
GS3 · Internal security / LWE
LWE has shrunk from nearly 200 districts to seven, showing that sustained state action can roll back insurgency.
Two-pronged strategy: security forces given the 'freedom to take every necessary decision', paired with development: roads, mobile towers, Eklavya schools and ITIs in affected areas.
GS3 · Linkages between development and extremism
The fall of LWE rests on two legs: firm security operations and the arrival of roads, towers and schools in the forest.

Restoring the state's reach: in affected areas 'life would come to a standstill after sunset' and Naxalites 'snatched away the people's right to vote'; their removal restores citizenship, not just order.
GS3 · LWE / GS2 · Democracy at the grassroots
Ending LWE restores the right to vote and move freely: security here is a precondition for democracy.

The ideological front: the PM said 'intellectual (dimagi) Naxalites' have infiltrated parties and organisations and are 'provoking people against the Constitution'; the battle shifts from forests to ideas.
GS3 · Role of non-state actors / ideology
With armed cadres defeated, the contest over LWE moves to ideas, where the state must win trust, not just territory.
Sacrifice and cost: 76 CRPF personnel were killed in Dantewada in 2010; for the first time in 47 years, no CRPF jawan lost his life on duty over the past year.
GS3 · Security forces / GS4 · Public service values
Not one CRPF jawan killed on duty in a year, a first in 47 years, shows how far the LWE theatre has changed.
keywords: Clearing an area of insurgents, holding it with forces, then building roads, schools and services
LWE's decline follows clear, hold, build: security first, then roads, towers and schools to hold the gains.
The absence of state services that extremists exploit
LWE grew where the state was absent; filling the governance deficit is the lasting cure.
Sympathy or support for LWE ideology among urban groups, distinct from armed cadres
The debate on 'urban Naxals' shows the line the state must hold between countering extremism and protecting dissent.
Roads and mobile towers reaching remote forest villages
Mobile towers in Bastar are last-mile connectivity that also serves as last-mile security.
data: LWE-affected districts: early 2000s, end of 2025, MHA review of February 2026
Government data cited by The Indian Express
LWE-affected districts fell from about 200 in the early 2000s to just seven in February 2026.
Fall in LWE-related incidents and resultant deaths since 2010
Government data cited by The Indian Express
LWE incidents and deaths have fallen by over four-fifths since 2010.
examples: Dantewada, 2010
76 CRPF personnel killed in a single encounter with Naxalites
GS3 · LWE as a security threat
The killing of 76 CRPF personnel in Dantewada in 2010 marked the peak of the LWE threat.
Eklavya schools and ITIs in LWE areas
Education and skilling as part of the counter-LWE strategy
GS4
GS3 · Development and extremism · GS4 · Inclusive governance
Eklavya schools and ITIs in Bastar show inclusive governance: the state wins tribal youth with classrooms, not only guns.
Mobile towers and roads in the forest
Connectivity extended to remote villages after operations
GS3 · Infrastructure for security
Roads and mobile towers in former Naxal areas turn military gains into lasting state presence.
pyqs: Determinants of LWE in eastern India.
Does tribal development policy reflect equity-based governance?
Threats from external state and non-state actors.

trend.t: LWE questions moved from causes (non-implementation of the Fifth Schedule, 2013; determinants in eastern India, 2020) to LWE as a development issue (2022) and then to the government's elimination target and measures (2025). Tribal development reappeared in 2026 as a question of equity-based governance.
trend.watch: LWE has been asked in 2013, 2020, 2022 and 2025, and the 2025 question was about the elimination target itself, so the 'after Naxalism' phase is the next likely angle: consolidation, development and rehabilitation in freed areas.
focus: Security plus development strategy and its results
Fifth Schedule, PESA and Forest Rights Act in freed areas
Rehabilitation of surrendered cadres and victims
Ideological contest: countering extremism while protecting dissent

potential: "Defeating armed insurgency is only half the task; winning the trust of the people is the other half." Discuss with reference to Left Wing Extremism in India. (15 marks)
Examine the role of infrastructure and welfare delivery in containing Left Wing Extremism. (10 marks)
What should be India's strategy to consolidate peace in areas freed from Left Wing Extremism? (15 marks)

practice.q: "Defeating armed insurgency is only half the task; winning the trust of the people is the other half." Discuss with reference to Left Wing Extremism in India.
parts: How the armed threat was defeated
Why trust is the other half

answer.t: LWE-affected districts fell from nearly 200 in the early 2000s to seven in February 2026, yet the PM warned in Bastar that the ideological danger 'has not completely disappeared'.

answer.h: How the armed threat was defeated

pts.t: Security forces were given the freedom to take every necessary decision, with sustained operations in core areas.
pts.ex: No CRPF jawan lost his life on duty over the past year, a first in 47 years.

pts.t: Support that LWE received from sympathisers within the system was targeted alongside armed cadres.
pts.ex: The PM's reference to stopping support from 'people sitting within the system'.

pts.t: Roads and mobile towers opened up the forests to forces and to the state.
pts.ex: Mobile towers and roads in Bastar.

pts.t: Eklavya schools and ITIs brought services into areas once cut off.
pts.ex: Eklavya model residential schools in tribal districts.

pts.t: Joint operations and shared intelligence across the Red Corridor states.
pts.ex: The MHA's periodic district-wise review of LWE affected areas.

pts.t: A time-bound goal created focus and accountability.
pts.ex: The March 31, 2026 'Naxal-free' target announced in the Lok Sabha.

answer.h: Why trust is the other half

pts.t: LWE grew from land alienation, displacement and a governance deficit; these do not end with operations.
pts.ex: Non-implementation of the Fifth Schedule was asked by UPSC in 2013.

pts.t: Unsettled forest rights and displacement for mining can revive grievance.
pts.ex: Forest Rights Act and PESA implementation gaps.

pts.t: Naxalites 'snatched away the right to vote'; elections and gram sabhas must now carry people's voice.
pts.ex: Strong turnout in former LWE areas as a test of trust.

pts.t: An ideology is countered by delivering justice and opportunity, not by force alone.
pts.ex: The PM's call to 'identify' intellectual Naxals.

pts.t: Countering extremist ideology must not chill legitimate criticism and tribal rights activism.
Surrendered cadres and victims need livelihoods, or the cycle restarts.
Shift from security camps to schools, health centres and banks in freed areas.
pts.ex: ITIs and Eklavya schools in Bastar.

pts.t: Implement PESA and the Forest Rights Act in letter and spirit.
pts.ex: Gram sabha consent for land and forest use.

pts.t: Skilling and local jobs to absorb young people.
Community policing and grievance redress to build confidence.
pts.ex: Civic action programmes of the CAPFs.

pts.t: Tribal languages and culture respected in schools and administration.
Keep the district-wise review going to prevent a relapse.

answer.t: The guns have largely fallen silent; India now has to make the state as present in a Bastar village's daily life as the security camp once was.

title: Raipur man who went to Russia for job lands in jail, now family seeks CM, police's help
syllabus: GS2 › Indian diaspora; welfare of Indians abroad · GS2 › Effect of policies and politics of other countries on India's interests · GS4 › Compassion towards the weaker sections; citizen-centric governance
summary: A Raipur store manager who left for Russia on a tourist visa after a job offer on Telegram says he is jailed on false charges and pressured to join the Russian army; his family has written to the CM, police and the PM's grievance portal.
ideas: A pattern, not a one-off: a 21-year-old from Bilaspur also went to Russia on a tourist visa after a Telegram job offer; neither family knew the nature of the work.
GS2 · Protection of Indians abroad
Repeated Telegram job offers that end in Russian detention point to an organised recruitment racket.
War's reach into Indian homes: men lured by jobs are allegedly pressured to sign consent to join the Russian military in the war against Ukraine.
GS2 · India–Russia relations / effect of conflicts on India
Indians forced into Russia's war show how distant conflicts reach poor families in India.
Slow and layered response: the complaint moves from the police commissionerate to the state home department to the MEA; the embassy said it was 'trying to ascertain the details'.
GS2 · Consular services / federal coordination
A family's plea passes through police, state and MEA, while a detained man waits.
Prevention gaps: tourist visas used for jobs, unregulated recruiters on social media and lack of pre-departure awareness among job seekers.
GS2 · Migration governance
Unregulated online recruitment needs the same scrutiny as licensed overseas recruiters.
keywords: Moving abroad out of economic pressure, often through risky channels
Distress migration through fake job offers turns aspiration into captivity.
A state's duty to assist its citizens in trouble abroad
Swift consular protection is the most visible duty a state owes its citizens abroad.
Administration designed around the citizen's needs, not files
A detained citizen's family should not have to knock on every door: that is the test of citizen-centric governance.
examples: Telegram job offers to Russia
Two Chhattisgarh men travelled on tourist visas and ended up detained or pressured to join the military
GS4
GS2 · Diaspora protection · GS4 · Compassion towards the weaker sections
The Chhattisgarh cases show why compassion towards the weaker sections must include citizens trapped abroad.
pyqs: Benefits of Indian diaspora in the West.
Diaspora as bridge turning heritage into geopolitical influence.

trend.t: Diaspora questions have looked at the benefits and influence of Indians abroad (2017, 2020, 2023, 2026); protection of vulnerable migrants has not been asked directly, but labour migration trends were (2015).
trend.watch: The diaspora was asked in 2023 and 2026, but only as an asset; the protection side, recruitment rackets and conflict zones, is a gap worth covering.
focus: Regulation of overseas recruiters and online offers

potential: "India's diaspora policy must protect the vulnerable migrant as much as it celebrates the successful one." Discuss. (10 marks)

title: Seema Mitra award for BSF, SSB, cops from 2027; Rajnath pays tribute to war heroes at Sherathang
where: Nation, page 6 (Press Trust of India, Hingalganj and Gangtok)
syllabus: GS3 › Security challenges and their management in border areas · GS3 › Various security forces and their mandate · GS4 › Public service values (dedication, sacrifice)
summary: West Bengal will institute a 'Seema Mitra' award from 2027 for BSF, SSB and state police guarding borders, and promised more frontier police stations; Defence Minister Rajnath Singh paid tribute to war heroes near Nathu La.
ideas: Centre–state cooperation at the border: West Bengal shares over 2,200 km with Bangladesh; the state will facilitate more police stations in frontier areas with infrastructure, logistics and manpower.
GS3 · Border management
Border management needs state police and central forces working as one, as West Bengal's frontier police stations aim to do.
Morale and recognition: an award for exceptional contributions by BSF, SSB and state police acknowledges hard frontier duty.
GS3 · Security forces / GS4 · Motivation
Recognition like the Seema Mitra award sustains morale in forces guarding remote borders.
Sacrifice remembered: at the Sherathang war memorial on the India–China border, the Defence Minister said 'every generation of Indians will remember your sacrifice'.
GS4 · Public service values
War memorials keep alive the values of duty and sacrifice that public service rests on.
keywords: Coordinated work of central forces, state police and civil agencies at borders
Integrated border management joins central forces and state police in one system.
examples: BSF and SSB
BSF guards the India–Bangladesh border; SSB the borders with Nepal and Bhutan
GS3 · Security forces and their mandate
BSF and SSB show India's border-specific force design: one force, one frontier.
pyqs: China and Pakistan borders; BADP and BIM.

trend.t: Border questions moved from strategy (2016) and crimes across borders (2020) to specific programmes such as BADP and border infrastructure (2024, 2026).
trend.watch: Border infrastructure and development programmes were asked in 2024 and 2026, so Centre–state cooperation and force welfare are useful supporting points.
focus: Morale and welfare of border forces

potential: Discuss the role of state governments in managing India's international land borders. (10 marks)

title: Equity at the margins: the Siddis
news: A 15-year-old Siddi girl won India's Youth Olympics judo medal; her community, a PVTG of about 12,959 in Gujarat, gets ST status in Saurashtra but not outside it.
syllabus: Inclusive governance; equity; compassion towards the weaker sections
link: Inclusive governance is not equal treatment but equitable opportunity: coaching camps, education and consistent legal status for a tiny, historically enslaved community. The Siddi youth who drop out of sports camps show that access without support is incomplete inclusion.
question: "Inclusive governance is judged by how the state treats those at the margins." Discuss with an example of a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group.

title: After the guns: winning trust in Bastar
news: The PM said armed Naxals have been wiped out but 'intellectual Naxals' must be defeated; LWE districts have fallen to seven.
syllabus: Good governance; inclusive governance; balancing security and rights
link: Security operations restore order, but legitimacy comes from schools, roads, gram sabhas and respect for tribal rights. The ethical task now is to counter extremist ideas without treating dissent or tribal assertion as disloyalty.
question: "The end of armed insurgency is the beginning of a test of governance." Discuss the ethical responsibilities of administrators in areas freed from Left Wing Extremism.

title: A family knocking on every door
news: The family of a Raipur man detained in Russia has written to the CM, police, embassies and the PM's grievance portal for help.
syllabus: Citizen-centric governance; compassion towards the weaker sections; accountability
link: A file passing from police to state home department to MEA is due process; for a family whose son is detained abroad, it is anguish. Citizen-centric governance means a single point of contact, time-bound updates and compassion in communication.
question: "Due process without compassion becomes indifference." Examine with reference to citizens in distress abroad.

title: A dormitory, not a slogan
news: Tamil Nadu employs 40.3% of India's directly employed women factory workers, helped by an innovative dormitory model adapted from China.
syllabus: Innovation and creativity in public service; Gender justice; Empathy
link: Empathy for women's real constraints, distance and safety, led to an innovative, practical fix rather than another incentive. Innovation in public service means seeing the barrier from the citizen's side and removing it.
question: "Innovation in public service begins with empathy for the citizen's real constraints." Discuss with examples.

title: Dollar investors, rupee investors
news: Amid calls to cut taxes for foreign investors, the Finance Minister asked: 'If you pitch for dollar investors, what about rupee investors?'
syllabus: Impartiality and non-partisanship; Fairness in public policy
link: Public policy must treat like cases alike: concessions that favour foreign over domestic investors for the same income break fairness and impartiality, even when the aim of attracting capital is legitimate. Good ends do not justify unequal means.
question: "Fairness in public policy means treating like cases alike." Examine with an example from economic policy.

title: Governing on trust
news: The Finance Minister said GST, income tax and other policies are framed on trusting businesses, farmers, taxpayers and citizens: 'That will remain our charter.'
syllabus: Public service values; Trust and citizen-centric governance; Accountability
link: A state that presumes honesty treats citizens as partners, not suspects, cutting harassment and compliance costs. Trust must be paired with accountability, so that honest citizens are freed while the few who abuse trust still face consequences.
question: "Trust-based governance must be balanced with accountability." Discuss with examples.

title: When rules outlive their purpose
news: Nagaland says the Protected Area Permit, framed for a different security era, and its convoluted process now keep tourists away from a peaceful state.
syllabus: Citizen-friendly administration; Efficiency in public service; Form versus substance
link: A rule is a means, not an end: when conditions change, administrators must review whether it still serves its purpose. Delays and last-minute relaxations show form winning over substance, and a citizen-centric administration fixes the process, not just the policy.
question: "Rules that outlive their purpose become obstacles to good governance." Discuss with examples.

title: Empathy across state lines
news: When Cyclone Murasu struck Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu sent 500 electricity workers in 25 teams to restore its neighbour's power.
syllabus: Empathy, compassion and tolerance towards the weaker sections; Public service values
link: Public service that ends at the state border is incomplete; helping a neighbouring state's people in a crisis shows empathy and solidarity as public values, beyond political rivalries.
question: "In a disaster, empathy must not stop at administrative boundaries." Discuss with examples.
